extraction.name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
extraction.description: IFEval is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark for large language models focused on a set of 'verifiable instructions' such as 'write in more than 400 words' and 'mention the keyword of AI at least 3 times'. It identifies 25 types of verifiable instructions and constructs around 500 prompts, with each prompt containing one or more verifiable instructions.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (Google and Yale University)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through few-shot prompting and manual curation. The process involved four steps: generating base prompts with randomly selected verifiable instructions, using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, rephrasing prompts to increase diversity, and manually checking and editing each rephrased prompt.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Prompts were synthetically generated using few-shot prompting with LLMs, combined with manual curation by the authors. The dataset consists of 541 prompts each containing one or more of 25 types of verifiable instructions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts were filtered for illogical combinations using few-shot prompting, then rephrased for diversity, and finally manually checked and edited one by one.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Instruction-following verification is performed programmatically using deterministic heuristics. A strict metric checks exact compliance, while a loose metric applies transformations (e.g., removing markdown font modifiers, removing first/last lines) to reduce false negatives.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The strict metric may produce false negatives (e.g., markdown-formatted responses not matching plain string checks). The loose metric reduces false negatives by applying transformations but may introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current implementation can be improved by increasing the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions and extending to multi-modal use cases. Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically, as edge cases exist where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of instruction-following ability of large language models. The benchmark is designed for automatic, reproducible, and unbiased evaluation of LLMs.

name.evidence: we introduce Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval) for large language models.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We alleviate these problems by creating our prompts through four steps. First, we generate a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt. Then, we use few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and remove them. As the third step, we apply another few-shot prompting based approach to rephrase each prompt, to increase the diversity of phrasing. Finally, we manually check and edit the rephrased prompts one by one.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: we found that there are still false negatives. For example, for a given verifiable instruction of 'end your email with: P.S. I do like the cake', a language model may follow the instruction by ending the email with 'P.S. **I do like the cake**' which has markdown tags... Although this loose instruction-following verification process reduces false negatives, it is likely to introduce false positives.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: It is important to note that while we focus on verifiable instructions, very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically – there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed... the current implementation of IFEval can be improved across many fronts. In particular: 1. Increase the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions. 2. Extend to multi-modal use cases.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we propose IFEval: Instruction-Following Eval, a benchmark to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions. These verifiable instructions are atomic instructions for which one can use a simple, interpretable, and deterministic program to verify if corresponding responses follow the instructions or not.
